back: Modal 'need' (e.g., 'needn't') doesn't change tense or add '-s' [12].
Needn't is most common in negative sentences [12].
Prefer 'need' as an ordinary verb ('Do you need to go?') over modal 'Need you go?' [12].
Used with negative words like 'hardly, never, nobody, only' (e.g., 'Nobody ever need know') [12].
Prefer 'don't need to' (e.g., 'You don't need to be over 18 to get into a nightclub') [12].
Prefer 'needn't' when the speaker decides something is unnecessary [12].
Prefer 'don't have to' when external rules make it unnecessary [12].
Use 'needn't' or 'don't have to' (NOT 'mustn't') (e.g., 'Volcanoes needn't erupt constantly') [12].
